body: Social Security Act 2018 section 84 provides that, in the disability allowance subpart, disability has the same meaning as in section 21(1)(h) of the Human Rights Act 1993.

Social Security Act 2018 section 85 provides that MSD may grant a disability allowance to or on account of a person who meets the eligibility criteria, or to the person's dependent spouse or dependent child, or who falls into a special category specified in regulations made under section 425. The criteria are that the person has a disability that reduces independent function so that the person requires ongoing support for everyday functions of life or ongoing supervision or treatment by a health practitioner; the disability is likely to continue for at least 6 months; the person receives a main benefit or the person's income, including spouse or partner income and any New Zealand superannuation or veteran's pension payable to the person or spouse or partner, is less than the appropriate amount in Schedule 5 Part 3; and the person has ongoing additional expenses arising from the disability, subject to Schedule 3 clause 19, with assistance available under the Act or any other enactment insufficient to meet them.

Social Security Act 2018 section 86 provides that a disability allowance is not payable for expenses arising from the disability of a resident assessed as requiring care where a funder pays some or all contracted care service costs under sections 54 to 58 of the Residential Care and Disability Support Services Act 2018, or for costs of residential care services for a person with a psychiatric, intellectual, physical, or sensory disability if the person's accommodation costs or care other than care in the person's own home are wholly or partly funded under the Pae Ora (Healthy Futures) Act 2022.

Social Security Act 2018 section 87 provides that MSD may refuse, reduce, or cancel a disability allowance if, for the disability that gives rise to the application, the applicant receives a disablement pension or entitlement under the Veterans' Support Act 2014, an entitlement under the Accident Compensation Act 2001, or an overseas pension or periodical allowance analogous to an entitlement to medical treatment, rehabilitation, other disability-related costs, or otherwise analogous to a disability allowance.

Social Security Act 2018 section 88 provides that, before granting a disability allowance, MSD may require the applicant, or the applicant's spouse or partner or child as applicable, to be examined by a prescribed health practitioner appointed by MSD.

Social Security Act 2018 Schedule 3 clause 19 provides that if a health or disability insurance payment is made to a person, on the person's behalf, for the person's benefit, or on behalf of or for the benefit of a family member, then for disability allowance purposes the person's additional disability expenses, or expenses from hospitalisation of the person's spouse or partner, are taken to be reduced to the extent MSD considers appropriate. MSD must have regard to the nature of the payment and those expenses.

Social Security Act 2018 Schedule 4 Part 9 clause 2, as amended on 1 April 2026 by the Social Security (Rates of Benefits and Allowances) Order 2026, sets the maximum rate of disability allowance under section 85 at $82.85 a week.

Social Security Act 2018 Schedule 5 Part 3, as amended on 1 April 2026 by the Social Security (Rates of Benefits and Allowances) Order 2026, sets disability allowance income limits per week: $696.60 for a single person aged 16 or 17 years without dependent children; $870.00 for any other single person without dependent children; $1,295.11 for a person in a relationship with or without dependent children; $971.51 for a sole parent with 1 dependent child; and $1,023.59 for any other sole parent.
